header.userPrompt:
Fix GitHub issue VirtusLab/orca#190: NoClassDefFoundError for orca/Flow$package$ on case-insensitive filesystems

On a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS default APFS, or a macOS directory bind-mounted into a Linux container), two runner tests fail:

```
==> X orca.runner.RoleSettingsFlowTest.an agents-only project file triggers discovery and appends the stack entries
    java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: orca/Flow$package$ (wrong name: orca/flow$package$)
==> X orca.runner.FlowLifecycleTest.--worktree: the run happens in the worktree, the invoking checkout is untouched, and a re-run returns to it
    java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: orca/Flow$package$ (wrong name: orca/flow$package$)
```

Reproduce on macOS at 75f620f7:

```
sbt "runner/testOnly orca.runner.RoleSettingsFlowTest orca.runner.FlowLifecycleTest"
```

## Cause

Two top-level-definition files in package `orca` compile to class names that differ only in case:

- `runner/src/main/scala/orca/flow.scala` → `runner/target/.../classes/orca/flow$package$.class`
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/Flow.scala` → `flow/target/.../classes/orca/Flow$package$.class`

When the JVM looks up `orca/Flow$package$.class` and the runner classes directory comes first on the classpath, the case-insensitive filesystem returns `flow$package$.class`, and class definition fails with the name mismatch. CI runs on Linux (case-sensitive), so it never sees this.

The same collision can surface in any consumer that puts both jars' contents into one directory on such a filesystem, not only in these tests.

## Fix

Rename one of the two files so that the generated `$package` class names no longer differ only in case.

resultJson.title: Fix NoClassDefFoundError on case-insensitive filesystems (#190)
resultJson.body:
Rename flow.scala to flowEntry.scala to resolve class name collision on case-insensitive filesystems.

Two top-level Scala files (`runner/src/main/scala/orca/flow.scala` and `flow/src/main/scala/orca/Flow.scala`) generated `$package` class files differing only in case. On case-insensitive filesystems (macOS, or Linux containers with macOS bind mounts), the JVM would look up one file and get the other, causing a class definition name mismatch.

The fix renames the runner's package object file to `flowEntry.scala`, eliminating the case collision. This ensures compatibility with case-insensitive filesystems without requiring case-sensitive mount options or special CI workarounds.
